heard: A letter from Nebraska found a stranger in Boston in five handoffs. No address. Each person could only mail it to someone they knew by first name. Stanley Milgram sent out 296 folders, all for one Boston stockbroker. You're in Omaha holding one, don't guess. Mail it to the friend most likely to know him, someone in Boston or in stocks. Why that works, you know about 100 people. They know 100 each. Two hops, 10 ,000. Five hops, 10 billion. But your friends all know each other. That overlap should kill it. It doesn't because of the friend who moved away. One cousin in Boston jumps 1 ,300 miles in a single hop. 64 folders made it with 5 .2 people in between. One in four came through a single shop owner in his hometown. So who would you mail it to first?
